- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-period, model lags in adjusting; forecast should be adjusted downward by 1–2% per day of sentiment decay.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility; use 10–15 day moving average of true prices as baseline for correction.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model tends to lag; forecast should be 1–2% above recent 7-day average to capture momentum.
